info.title: The Plunge on the Boardwalk

info.title: Battery Station on Front Street
info.citation: “Battery Station on Front Street.” Leonard, Diane. SCPL Local History. https://history.santacruzpl.org/omeka/items/show/3594. Accessed 12 Nov. 2026.
info.how_location_was_determined: Alfred C. Handley's Battery Station was located at 325-335 Front Street immediately adjacent to the Jensen Brothers Ford garage at Front and Cooper Streets in downtown Santa Cruz.

photos.albumTitle: Menlo Park Historical Photo Archive
photos.title: img211 - Google Map of the area south of SLAC overlayed with the map of Searsville from Drothy F. Regnery, The History of Jasper Ridge (c. 1991), p. 97. The scaling is dominated by matching the Mayfield-Searsville Road on Regnery’s map to Sand Hill Road on the Google map. Dennis Martin’s Lane (sometimes called Church Lane), which is seen to cut through SLAC at Sector 16, conforms to today’s Ansel Lane. The old Jane Goodale Primate Center is on Ansel Lane near what is marked on the map as House 2. There is still a gate at the SLAC perimeter fence where Ansel Lane meets the SLAC Klystron Gallery south road. Nothing remains of Dennis Martin’s Lane north of SLAC.

info.title: Swinging Bridge, Santa Cruz
info.description: A swinging bridge over the San Lorenzo River at Big Trees Park in California. Printed on the front of the card, "LITHO BRITTON & REY, SAN FRANCISCO, CAL. 2009 Swinging Bridge, Santa Cruz, California."
info.rights: This postcard is the property of the Santa Cruz Public Libraries, California.
info.how_location_was_determined: The card depicts the suspension footbridge across the San Lorenzo River at the entrance to the Santa Cruz Big Trees Grove in Felton, now part of Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park.
info.how_year_was_determined: This chromolithograph postcard has a divided back introduced after March 1907 and was printed by Britton and Rey of San Francisco before the firm merged in 1915.

Loveland Post Office (c. 1900) - Jane Loveland was appointed to her position by Senator Leland Stanford. She was the state's first lady postmaster. The building (constructed in 1892) was on Golder Lane, near the railroad depot, now Santa Cruz Ave. Loveland, who was given the building when she retired, moved it a few blocks west and converted it into her residence. In the photo to the right is the Palace Market meat wagon.

info.how_location_was_determined: This studio portrait of Christiana Felt and infant Arthur Felt comes from the Felt family collection in Live Oak, Santa Cruz County, though the catalog coverage field lists Santa Clara County.
info.how_year_was_determined: Although the metadata coverage lists the 1870s, the puffed sleeves on Christiana Felt's dress and the companion 1880s family portrait showing young Arthur Felt as a boy indicate an 1880s date.

info.title: On Bikes
info.citation: “On Bikes.” Poandl, Pam. SCPL Local History. https://history.santacruzpl.org/omeka/items/show/3628. Accessed 12 Nov. 2026.
info.how_location_was_determined: The metadata places this photograph in Santa Clara County, and the coast redwood trees and dirt trail in the background indicate the Santa Cruz Mountains along the western border of Santa Clara County.
info.how_year_was_determined: The metadata coverage indicates the 1910s, and Florence and Grace Mosher wear the exact same hats and blouses seen across the rest of the Pam Poandl contributor series dated to 1913.
